clue.text: Support retired people making a verbal onslaught

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for support is read backwards

parts.note: support means aid
a tribe is a people

explanation.surface: Backing for pensioners turns into a fierce spoken attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' means withdrawn, so the support word is turned round before the people word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, abusive tirade, a sustained spoken attack.

clue.text: Joining medico in French church would be wet!

parts.note: medico means doctor, abbreviated DR
en is the French for in

explanation.surface: A doctor entering a French church would find it damp.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench is to soak thoroughly, to make very wet.

clue.text: Hope for some sort of praise

indicators.note: sort here means to rearrange, so the letters of praise are mixed up

explanation.surface: Wishing for a little commendation.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim at or long for an achievement.

clue.text: The Right are right less often

parts.note: R again for right
R again for right

explanation.surface: Political conservatives are correct only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer means occurring less frequently.

clue.text: Skip the queen and the knave

parts.note: to skip is to leap or bound
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: Leaving out the card-game's queen and jack.
explanation.walkthrough: The playing-card picture misleads: knave here means a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounder is a dishonourable man, a cad or rogue.

clue.text: Soldiers late for a meal

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a crossword stand-in for soldiers
late means past, as in former

explanation.surface: Troops arriving behind schedule for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal or feast.

clue.text: Cut up over underground workers, they want satisfactory answers

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for cut is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
miners work underground

explanation.surface: Chopping above pit workers who demand good replies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA, placed over MINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners mark tests and look for correct responses from candidates.

clue.text: A form occasioning much disgust

parts.note: a version is one form of something

explanation.surface: A document provoking great revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or repugnance.

clue.text: Note the revolutionary may well appear restrained

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a red is a revolutionary or communist

explanation.surface: Observe how the radical looks held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up with a rope, so held in check.

clue.text: Where one might buy a ruler without hesitation-and one with hesitation

indicators.note: without means the word for hesitation is removed from the ruler

parts.note: an emperor is a ruler
er is a sound of hesitation
one is the Roman numeral I
um is another sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A shopping tip about a monarch who speaks fluently and one who stammers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the first hesitation from the ruler; 'one' is used twice, once in the definition and once as the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop or trading centre, a place for purchasing goods.

clue.text: Dormant talent may be developed

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of talent being worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Unused gifts can be cultivated.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but not yet active, like something lying asleep.

clue.text: Sound lot arranging a celebration

indicators.note: sound signals a word that is pronounced like another

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A healthy batch arranging a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festival or outdoor fundraising fair.

clue.text: The case for providing transport to the crest

parts.note: a cart is a means of transport
a ridge is a crest of a hill

explanation.surface: An argument for laying on a vehicle up to the hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a casing holding a bullet and charge, or ink, film and so on.

clue.text: The subject of children

definitions.meaning: the topic or matter under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a topic for debate, and in legal language a person's issue are their descendants.

clue.text: A boom? Dispute that

definitions.meaning: a pole or ... on a ship's rigging, such as one along the foot of a sail
to argue or box, as in sparring

explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole such as a mast or boom; to spar is to wrangle or argue.

clue.text: Strive always to be dressed in bluish grey

indicators.note: dressed in means clothed by, so one piece sits inside the colour word

parts.note: perse is a dark greyish-blue colour
ever means always

explanation.surface: Try always to wear blue-grey clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep trying in spite of difficulty.

clue.text: Looks to foreign money-a quite unacceptable thing

parts.note: to eye is to look at, so eyes means looks
ore is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone gazing at overseas currency, which proves disagreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly and offensive to look at.

clue.text: Newly-built homes-and so good looking

indicators.note: newly built suggests the letters of homes and being reconstructed

explanation.surface: Freshly constructed houses are therefore attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means attractive in appearance.

clue.text: They won't pay cash for horses

definitions.meaning: people who put purchases on account rather than paying money

explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers who charge goods to an account avoid paying cash, and chargers are knights' war horses.

clue.text: Stuck with the novel he'd read

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of he'd read appear in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone persevered with the book he had been reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhered means clung or stayed fast, as glue does.

clue.text: A weapon that causes many disquiet

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
to irk is to annoy or disturb

explanation.surface: An arms device that unsettles lots of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a Scottish dagger.

clue.text: Make short work of the tall grass

definitions.meaning: a tall marsh plant with hollow stems

explanation.definitionFit: To rush a task is to hurry it through, and a rush is a tall waterside plant like a grass.

clue.text: Send out wrong aid and there's censure about it

indicators.note: about means the censure word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to rate is an old verb for to scold

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of aid are put out of order

explanation.surface: Distributing faulty assistance and getting criticised for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles aid, and 'about' wraps the old verb for scold round the result; rate in that sense is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to emit heat, light or energy outwards.

clue.text: Endeavour to make a virtuous man split

parts.note: ST, saint, is a virtuous man
to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: Trying to break up a good man.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to try hard.

clue.text: Following a bizarre trend-getting really keen

indicators.note: bizarre means odd, so the letters of trend are jumbled

explanation.surface: Copying an odd fashion makes one very enthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionately eager.

clue.text: A portion of sea-food or sea-fish

definitions.text: A portion of sea-food or sea-fish

indicators.note: a portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A serving of fish from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'A' as the definition, which cannot be right; the whole clue defines, since the hidden fish is itself a portion of seafood. The letters run 'sea-fooD OR SEa'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorse is a young cod, so it is a sea-fish and a portion of seafood.

clue.text: Most important, and correspondingly rubricated?

definitions.meaning: memorable or special, as a notable day
rubricated means marked in red, and the correspondence is a written message

explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special one, from saints' days printed in red ink in calendars; red plus a written message gives the second reading.

clue.text: Quarters are given up, so remove

indicators.note: in a down clue given up means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: E and S are two compass quarters, east and south

explanation.surface: Lodgings are surrendered, so clear out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' reverses both pieces as one run, as a down entry read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or delete.

clue.text: This will start when duck preen perhaps

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of preen may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A bird grooming itself is about to begin something.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O; the opening batsman starts the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener is whatever begins proceedings, such as a cricket batsman who starts the innings.

clue.text: The head holding a painter back is a pest!

indicators.note: holding means the head word contains the other pieces

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword painter

indicators.note: back means the little word is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone clutching an artist from behind is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only the little word round; pate is an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off another organism, and figuratively is a sponger or pest.

clue.text: A woman in extremity-turned out

indicators.note: in means the woman is placed inside the other word

parts.note: an end is an extremity
Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman at her wits' end was overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed or resulted, as events turn out.

clue.text: Housing for male adults in view

indicators.note: in places the adults inside the word for a view

parts.note: a tenet is a view or belief
men are male adults

explanation.surface: Accommodation for grown men on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a block of flats, a building for dwelling in.
